patch.value: GH-1679: SDK and CLI item history have no producer cursor, so paging backwards through a long history requests an ever-larger newest suffix per page

GitHub issue #1679 (reported 2026-11-06 against 2026.11.5 from an SDK adoption review of the fleet). HistoryCommandOptions exposes limit and order but no producer cursor, and HistoryResult returns no continuation (dist/sdk/query/history.d.ts). Public output cursors page an already-produced projection, so they do not bound the historical read. A consumer paging backwards through a long item history must request an ever-larger newest suffix for each older page, then verify and filter it. The concrete consumer is pm-web's item-history panel (src/services/item-history.ts), which requests successively larger suffixes. Proposal: opaque bounded backwards and forwards item-history paging in the SDK and CLI. The continuation is bound to the item, order, projection and a verified stream boundary. Each page returns bounded rows, explicit completeness and omission receipts, and a safe stale_cursor refusal. Pages stay stable under appends where safe, and compaction, rewrite or truncation ambiguities are refused. The producer cursor stays distinct from the output cursor contract. Duplicate check: searched history cursor paging; pm-c3aiik (GH-1325, closed) fixed history diff cursor advancement, pm-dfg0 (closed) list/search/context cursors, pm-8s53lj (open) newest-page retention for comments/notes, pm-tuadp2 (open) delta projections, GH-1470 replay infrastructure. None provides a producer cursor over one item's history stream. No benchmark was run; evidence is declaration and consumer-code analysis.

HistoryCommandOptions accepts an opaque producer cursor for backwards and forwards paging and HistoryResult returns a continuation bound to the item, order, projection and a verified stream boundary; Each page reads a bounded number of entries regardless of history length, proven by a work-bound spec over a long history; Concurrent appends between pages neither skip nor duplicate certified rows, and a cursor for another item, a tampered cursor, or a stream compacted or rewritten since issue is refused with a typed stale_cursor error; The producer cursor is distinct from the output cursor contract and works in JSON and TOON through CLI, SDK and MCP
Backwards item-history paging reads a bounded page per call through an opaque producer cursor that refuses stale or foreign continuations
